qualified_claims: Equal-magnitude current vertical groundwater forcing is allocation-sign-asymmetric in the tested Ribasim v2026.1.1 topology.
Current Basin infiltration enters the implicit negative-forcing term and can be completely attenuated by low_storage_factor=0 while accepted storage memory remains admitted.
Current Basin drainage enters the explicit positive-forcing term without the low_storage_factor multiplier and directly increases managed availability.

With the same accepted state and forcing magnitude, positive drainage fills the remaining 0.009627619 m3/day root deficit and allocates approximately 7.9904148932 m3/day to the lower-priority external demand, while equal-magnitude infiltration leaves external allocation at zero.
The accepted storage draw is unchanged across all three cases, isolating forcing representation rather than changing accepted memory.

mathematical_contract.positive_forcing: Basin drainage contributes to the volume-conservation right-hand side as explicit positive forcing.
mathematical_contract.negative_forcing: Basin infiltration contributes through alpha * implicit_negative_forcing, with alpha = low_storage_factor.
mathematical_contract.tested_directional_effect: For equal magnitude F, +F is admitted directly while -F can be forecast-attenuated through alpha.

boundaries: This is allocation forecast asymmetry, not physical non-conservation or one-way groundwater physics.
The result is specific to the tested Basin drainage/infiltration representation and topology.
No claim that all Ribasim positive/negative processes have identical treatment.
No production prescription or production admission.
downstream: Release prospectively frozen DUMMY-20H9 to bridge positive groundwater forcing into the actual RibaMod t=24 allocation output.
